standard_prerequisites.name: The comparison of a module with its twist by a Cartier divisor, giving the inclusion of the de Rham complex
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: More on Flatness, Section \ref{flat-section-eta} (invoked at proof line 2423)
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the reference for the canonical inclusion $\Omega^p_{X/S} \subset \Omega^p_{X/S}(Y)$ and the statement that the differentials have no nonzero local sections supported on $Y$.

standard_prerequisites.name: The shift convention for cochain complexes
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Homology, definition homology-definition-shift-cochain (invoked at proof line 2466)
standard_prerequisites.use: It fixes the sign of the differential on $\Omega^\bullet_{Y/S}[-1]$, which the author matches with the forced sign in the Leibniz rule for the log complex.

standard_prerequisites.name: The local splitting hypothesis defining log poles
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter derham.tex, the assumption stated in the statement (used at proof lines 2405-2417)
standard_prerequisites.use: For a local equation $f$ it gives $\Omega_{X/S,y} = \mathcal{O}_{X,y}\mathrm{d}f \oplus M$ with torsion free exterior powers, from which $\Omega^p_{Y/S,y} = \wedge^p(M/fM)$ and the absence of sections supported on $Y$ follow.

core_obligations: Unpack the hypothesis: write $\Omega_{X/S,y} = \mathcal{O}_{X,y}\mathrm{d}f \oplus M$ and $\Omega^p_{X/S,y} = \wedge^{p-1}(M)\mathrm{d}f \oplus \wedge^p(M)$ for a local equation $f$, deduce $\Omega^p_{Y/S,y} = \wedge^p(M)/f\wedge^p(M)$, and conclude that $\Omega^p_{X/S}$ has no nonzero local sections supported on $Y$, so that $\Omega^p_{X/S} \subset \Omega^p_{X/S}(Y)$ (proof lines 2405-2422).

Construct the log complex: on an affine open $U$ with $Y \cap U = V(f)$ take the submodule of $\Omega^p_{X/S}(Y)|_U$ generated by $\Omega^p_{X/S}|_U$ and $\mathrm{d}\log(f)\wedge\Omega^{p-1}_{X/S}$, note that replacing $f$ by $uf$ changes $\mathrm{d}\log(f)$ by a section of $\Omega_{X/S}$, and glue these local submodules to a quasi-coherent submodule sitting between $\Omega^p_{X/S}$ and $\Omega^p_{X/S}(Y)$ (proof lines 2423-2438).

Define the residue map $\mathrm{Res}(\eta' + \mathrm{d}\log(f)\wedge\eta) = \eta|_{Y\cap U}$ and show it is surjective with kernel $\Omega^p_{X/S}$, using that a form restricting to zero on $Y$ can be written as $\mathrm{d}f\wedge\eta' + f\eta''$, which yields the short exact sequence of the statement in each degree (proof lines 2439-2457).

Define the differentials: use the de Rham differential on $\Omega^p_{X/S}$ and set $\mathrm{d}(\mathrm{d}\log(f)\wedge\eta) = -\mathrm{d}\log(f)\wedge\mathrm{d}\eta$; note that the sign is forced by the Leibniz rule and is compatible with the shifted differential $-\mathrm{d}_{Y/S}$, so that the sequences of complexes are exact as claimed (proof lines 2458-2468).
proof_roadmap: The local splitting hypothesis and its consequences (proof lines 2405-2422).
Construction and gluing of the log complex (proof lines 2423-2438).
The residue map and the degreewise exactness (proof lines 2439-2457).
The differentials and the sign (proof lines 2458-2468).
difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs the de Rham complex of log poles along an effective Cartier divisor and exhibits it as the middle term of a canonical short exact sequence of complexes (statement lines 2390-2402). The proof unpacks the local splitting hypothesis to identify the relative differentials on the divisor and to see that nothing is supported on it, builds the log complex locally out of the de Rham complex and logarithmic derivatives of a defining equation, glues those local pieces, defines the residue map with the required kernel, and fixes the differential by the sign forced from the Leibniz rule and the shift convention. The local construction plus the sign analysis is the substance, so the claim is H2.
